title: Does Personalized Pricing Increase Competition? Evidence from NIL in College Football
eligible_reason: Single adoption date. The NIL policy takes effect for all programs at T_NIL (2021); the DiD in NIL_functions.R::compute_did_effects defines NIL = 1[year >= T_NIL] and treat = NIL x domestic (international recruits as controls), estimated by feols with position FE, recruit covariates (rating, rank, height, weight) and clustering by position; event study i(year, domestic, ref=2020) with year FE. No unit-specific adoption dates. Other estimators are IPW/AIPW/causal-forest treatment-effect estimators and conference-level DiDs with I(year>=2021).
design_notes: Recruit-level data from collegefootballdata.com (2013-2024 classes) plus Knight-Newhouse spending, College Scorecard, DMA/TV data. NIL_ATE.R: compute_treatment_effects (IPW, AIPW via grf, OLS) and compute_did_effects (pre/post 2021 x domestic). NIL_regressions.R: draft outcome regressions (Table 6), betting spread regressions (Table 12). Appendix.R: conference-level pre/post regressions.
estimators_reported: two-group pre/post DiD with covariates (feols/fepois, position FE)
data_files: data/*.csv (28 scraped CFBD files, spending, TV, DMA geojson); College Scorecard files must be downloaded separately
screener_notes: Screened from package only (_readme, NIL_functions.R, NIL_regressions.R, Appendix.R). Not staggered.
software_notes: R 4.4.1: fixest, grf, WeightIt, MatchIt, binsreg, rdrobust; Python notebook for scraping
